text: The Seaburger dies today.
Are we going to leave Paris now?
I'm sorry, Anne, but I must go back to the Abbott's house.
No, Monsieur, no!
I must! Now, my friend should be there by now.
He may know who the Seaburger is.
If you go back there, they'll arrest you.
No, they won't. The Doctor should be able to stop them.
They'll recognize you before you can find him.
The Captain of the Guard, or Monsieur Colbert?
Perhaps if I disguise.
See if we can find some other clothes.
Well, this should do.
Don't, Monsieur.
Yes, well, never mind.
Now, if I can find a hat...
Yes, well, I don't think the Captain will recognize me in this.
If we ally ourselves to the Dutch in their conflict with Spain,
the common cause will unify the country
and prevent further civil strife.
Oh, surely the marriage between Henry of Navarre
and His Majesty's sister
have already put an end to the disturbances.
For how long?
As I have pointed out frequently,
in this chamber,
it would take but one small incident,
and the whole of Paris could be in uproar.
Incidents occur daily, yet still the city does not rise.
If we allied ourselves with the Dutch,
even those incidents would not take place.
My Admiral has a good point there.
Pray accept it, Marshal,
and let us finish with this tedious business.
Your Majesty, France cannot afford this war.
So we are told frequently by our mother.
The recent conflict in France
has brought us almost to ruin.
There is no money to pay for the forces
that would be needed to wage war with Spain.
But is it not so that under the treaty signed at Blois,
the English will come to our assistance?
Not you as well, my little counsellor.
The Admiral and the Marshal quarrel well enough without assistance.
I apologize, sir.
I had hoped to end the deadlock between them.
It was good to hear a different voice.
So Elizabeth of England has agreed to help us.
Does anyone here trust her?
She breaks more promises than I do.
She has no love for Spain.
She has yet to come out into the open and say so.
However, if Your Majesty is so eager to fight this war,
perhaps we could raise the money
by leasing the Alpine hunting grounds to Italy.
Do you mock me, Marshal?
Of course not, sire.
But the war will have to be paid for.
Some sacrifices will have to be made.
We will give away nothing of our land.
Besides, the bears there are French.
They might not like to be sold.
True.
Next winter you will accompany us on our hunt.
Your Majesty, there is enough money in France to finance the war.
Enough of this war. I am bored of Spain.
But I beg to advise, Your Majesty...
No, Admiral, please. Talk of it some other time.
War is so tedious.
Move to matters closer to us.
If the King refuses to make war,
may it please God that another war will not be forced on him.
But it will not be easy to renounce.
Then you must come with me.
But they'll arrest me at the abbot's house.
They won't.
Now, look, I'm almost certain that my friend is pretending to be the abbot.
Now, he'll make sure that no harm comes to you.
Oh, but, Monsieur...
Now, you must trust me. I'll take care of you.
You've been very kind to me, Monsieur, but...
Well, I'm afraid to go back to that house.
Look, I'll be with you.
Besides, you won't stay here, so where will you go?
All right, I'll come with you.
Look, if anything happens on the way to the abbot's,
if I'm recognized, then we'll have to run.
Now, you must come back here. Do you understand?
Well, suppose they catch me?
No, they won't. I'll be the one they chase.
Now, if you come back here, I'll know where to find you.
And I can join you as soon as possible.
How much longer are the Huguenots to suffer these frequent violations of their rights?
The treaty drawn up by the Queen Mother to conclude the religious difficulties of the country
was generous in the extreme to the free thinkers.
Words were spoken. Signatures were exchanged.
But they did not prevent many acts against the Huguenots.
Do you question the promises of the Queen Mother, Admiral?
It is easy to promise. You speak truth.
Why is it not possible for our counselors to talk without quarreling?
Sire, it is imperative that the religious differences of the country
be fully discussed.
Admiral, grant me but a few days' war in which to amuse myself,
and then I promise you, as king,
that I shall make you happy and all those of your religion.
Kings are recognized only by the power they wield.
The Queen Mother seems to claim this power.
Take care, Your Majesty, that it does not prove detrimental to yourself and to France.
Your Majesty!
Never, no more!
Marshal, this meeting is over.
Since my noble mother seems fit to depart, let us do likewise.
We meet again on the feast of St. Bartholomew,
so until the day after tomorrow, let us enjoy ourselves.
Was that wise?
To insult the Queen will only make her work harder against you.
It was time her power was challenged.
The king still fears his mother.
Surely this may damage all for which you've worked so hard.
Let us hope not.
Admiral, come with us.
We are going to play tennis.
Your Majesty, I must beg to be excused.
I have work which must be done.
Oh, my dear Admiral, we are pleased with you.
Since now our mother will not speak to us for the rest of today,
you will come with us.
I have a new racket I want you to see. Come.
We have to wait in here. The abbot cannot be disturbed.
Yes, but I must speak to him. It's most important.
You do not understand, young man.
The abbot is saying his office.
His what?
His office. We cannot disturb him while he is at prayer.
Well, how long is he going to be?
You must curb your impatience, young man.
If you will tell me what your business is,
then perhaps I can help you.
I have a message for the abbot
concerning a man who is to die today.
If it is a case of the last sacraments,
then there is no need to trouble the abbot.
I myself will come with you.
Well, no. I mean, it's very kind of you, but...
Is there something more?
Well, yes, and I can only discuss it with the abbot.
What is this, my lord abbot?
Doctor!
Doctor!
Silence!
Who is this man?
And why does he disturb my peace?
It appears he comes from a dying man.
Well, I...
I've brought back the servant who ran away.
You have done well, my son.
Father, you may leave us.
I will settle this matter.
Very well, my lord abbot.
I felt you would be safer here
as Bondo waits for the sea beggar.
Father, I have a word with you.
The young man has returned the girl to us, Marshal.
What girl?
The one who lodged with the sea beggar.
Ah, she is of no importance.
I must speak with you alone.
Very well. Take the girl and wait outside.
I'll tell you later.
Of course, I never fail, neither do my servants.
Is Bondo ready?
Bondo has been prepared for the last two hours.
Quick, quick, I must tell Nicholas.
Is the sea beggar on his way home?
I don't know.
The king delayed him after the council.
He had seen fit to insult the queen mother
and his majesty was naturally pleased with him.
De Cullingly will allow no one to take him away from his work.
I think we can take it he is on his way by now.
The girl, the servant who ran away.
Colbert, how dare you interrupt us?
But she's with the Englishman from the Admiral's house.
I've just seen them.
What?
The Englishman with the girl.
He's the one who was with the Huguenots.
Who did he say he was?
I never asked him.
Catch them back.
I sent the guards after them.
He was taken around the side door.
My Lord Abbott, what mistake have you perpetrated now?
He could not hear what was being said.
I sent him out of the room.
In any case, it is too late for him to warn the Admiral.
For your sake, it had better be.
Come away!
Nicholas, quickly, it's the Admiral.
Be quiet, what's wrong?
The plot.
Yes, it's the Admiral they're going to kill.
De Cullingly.
Today, now.
But how?
I don't know, but you've got to warn him.
He's at the Louvre. There's a council meeting.
No, it's over.
They're going to kill him on the way back.
Where?
The room.
Saint-Germain?
They've passed Saint-Germain.
Yes.
Stay here.
We must get him to a surgeon.
... further.
Due to your stupidity, the Englishman has had a chance to warn him.
I said he did not hear anything.
Then why did he run off?
I don't know.
If this should go wrong, you are to blame.
And you will be the one to answer for it.
The Cardinal...
... is in Rome and cannot help you now.
If de Cullingly is delayed by the King,
then the news of his death will be delayed also.
Bondo is an excellent marksman.
You know that there is only one thing for us to do,
and that is to wait.
Meantime, I will retire to my room.
You will not.
You will wait here with me.
The attempt has failed.
Bondo is caught.
He ran away.
The Admiral was only wounded, not killed.
The beggar lives.
You have failed.
Call the guards.
Father Abbott, since you came, everything that had been so carefully planned has gone wrong.
This man is a traitor to the Queen.
Mr. de Cullingly?
I'm waiting.
I'm sorry, Your Majesty, but the news I have must be given first to the King.
Now, what's the matter?
Why must I always be interrupted?
And I was winning.
Your pardon, sir, but I bring news of the greatest importance.
Well, what is it?
Admiral de Cullingly has been severely wounded.
Someone tried to shoot him.
Your Majesty, the Admiral is badly hurt.
What happened?
The assassins were waiting in the Rue des Forces Saint-Germain.
As we came down the street, they fired at him.
Were they caught?
No, sir.
We searched the house and found the weapon.
The men had gone.
Well, they must be found.
An inquiry.
Call the council.
The Admiral's assassins must be caught and punished.
Council!
My little father.
I will see you avenged.
I'll be to my own room.
Help me up.
No, Admiral, wait for the surgeon.
He'll be here soon.
Why did they do it?
Are you sure we should not take him to his own room?
He's lost so much blood.
Go and wait for the surgeon.
Bring him straight in.
Yes, sir.
Nicholas, I'm sorry.
I tried to tell Gaston. He wouldn't listen to me.
I know. He told me.
I knew that the sea beggar was going to be killed.
Until this morning, I didn't know who that was.
I could have told you.
How did you find out?
When I ran away from you yesterday, I went to the abbot's house.
The doctor wasn't there.
But I overheard some men talking about the sea beggar.
Who were they?
Well, one of them was the same man who came to see the abbot this morning.
So the abbot is behind this.
No, the abbot is the doctor.
Now that I've seen him, I'm certain of it.
He's just pretending to be the abbot. That's all.
Now, listen, Stephen.
Obviously, he's very weak.
The king has called for an inquiry, but it won't do any good.
What do you mean?
As I left the Louvre, I heard that some of our men have taken the law into their own hands.
How?
The abbot of Amboise was murdered just outside his own house.
What?
The abbot is dead, and they're blaming it on the Huguenots.
But who's the abbot?
The king has summoned the council. I must return to the Louvre.
Take care of him, Nicholas.
Marshal, since you claim to know nothing of this attempted assassination,
I have a special charge for you.
You will be responsible for the admiral's safety.
Empty the street of Cathalex, station your men around his house,
and mark me well.
If anything further,
happens to him, you pay with your head.
We do not need the marshal's protection, sire.
To drive Cathalex from their homes will only make them hate us even more.
Is that possible?
Your concern for your friends, does you credit, sire?
I gave you an order. See, it is done.
But, sire...
Not another word!
I've had enough of your bickering. Leave me.
You summoned the council?
I gave orders I was to be left alone.
Without my knowledge or consent?
I asked to be left alone, mother.
To fret over your friend, the admiral.
You are the king.
Yes, I am the king! I have to be obeyed!
Now, keep out of my sight, unless you care to end your days in a convent.
I would wish you have the courage, my son.
I have but to give the order.
Summon your guards.
Have me arrested.
But you had better have a good reason for the council.
And for the people.
The attempted assassination of my admiral.
By you and Tervan.
Do you deny it, madame?
No.
Have a care.
I believe what I say. I shall send Tervan to the block.
He would execute the Martian of France for doing his duty.
Duty? He's an assassin!
He tried to rid you of a dangerous enemy.
Sir Coligny is my friend.
You, madame, are my enemy.
Madame?
No. If ever I am a word to you.
Look at these before you decide who are your enemies.
You think the Huguenots would stop at killing me.
They want your blood, too.
So you keep telling me every day of my life.
Why?
I protect them. They're all my subjects. What are they to gain?
Until now, nothing.
And now?
We have a Protestant prince in Paris, Henry of Navarre.
You think they'd ever take it for your protection?
Now that one of their own is within grasp of the throne?
The Huguenots must have done it.
They shouldn't be allowed to come here. They've done it.
The Huguenots would stop at nothing.
They'd even kill our priest.
They all believe the Huguenots killed him.
What have they done?
The Huguenots murdered him.
No, they didn't. They just took him down.
But he'll be responsible.
After him, George, catch him!
